trial_title: Testosterone Gel in Preventing Weakness Caused by Steroid Therapy in Men With Glioma
brief_summary:
RATIONALE: Testosterone gel may be effective in preventing or lessening muscle weakness caused by steroid therapy in men receiving glucocorticoids for newly diagnosed high-grade glioma.

PURPOSE: This randomized clinical trial is studying how well testosterone gel works in preventing weakness caused by steroid therapy in men receiving glucocorticoids for newly diagnosed high-grade glioma.

eligibility_table.criterion: Newly diagnosed high-grade glioma, including the following subtypes:
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has anaplastic astrocytoma, which is a subtype of high-grade glioma.
The patient has anaplastic astrocytoma, meeting the inclusion criteria.
The patient does not have anaplastic oligodendroglioma; they have anaplastic astrocytoma.
The patient does not have glioblastoma multiforme; they have anaplastic astrocytoma.

eligibility_table.criterion: Requires dexamethasone at a dose of > 4 mg/day to control symptoms of tumor-related edema at time of study enrollment AND has been on a stable dose of steroids for ≥ 5 days prior to study enrollment
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is on high-dose steroids, but the specific dose and duration of stable dosing are not provided.
There is no information indicating that the patient has completed ≥ 80% of prescribed radiotherapy.

eligibility_table.criterion: Hypogonadal, defined as serum testosterone level < 350 ng/dL
eligibility_table.justification: No serum testosterone level is provided to assess hypogonadal status.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's serum testosterone level currently < 350 ng/dL?

eligibility_table.criterion: No history of prostate or breast cancer
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has no reported history of prostate or breast cancer.

eligibility_table.criterion: No benign prostatic hypertrophy requiring therapy OR AUA score of ≥ 8
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding benign prostatic hypertrophy or AUA score.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have an AUA score of <8?

eligibility_table.justification: No PSA level is provided to assess eligibility.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's most recent PSA level ≤ 4 ng/mL?

eligibility_table.justification: Karnofsky performance status is not provided; unable to assess.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a Karnofsky performance status score of 60 or higher?

eligibility_table.criterion: Able to keep daily records or has a care provider that agrees to keep daily records of drug administration
eligibility_table.justification: Patient can likely keep daily records or has a care provider.

eligibility_table.criterion: No clinical history of congestive heart failure requiring therapy
eligibility_table.justification: No history of congestive heart failure mentioned.

eligibility_table.criterion: No psychotic disorder requiring active treatment
eligibility_table.justification: No psychotic disorder requiring treatment is noted.

eligibility_table.criterion: No structured exercise program involving exercise for > 3 hours/week
eligibility_table.justification: No information on structured exercise program is provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient engaged in a structured exercise program involving exercise for ≤3 hours/week in the past month?

eligibility_table.justification: No lab values provided to assess for polycythemia.

eligibility_table.criterion: More than 6 months since prior androgen therapy
eligibility_table.justification: No information on prior androgen therapy is provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient received any androgen therapy within the last 6 months?
